archetype.name: Retooling (shot-making, no backbone)
archetype.definition: A team coming off a 26-win season that has a genuine top-of-position star in Cooper Flagg and a wing group worth building around, but a frontcourt and backcourt that are not yet good enough to turn efficient shooting into a winning margin.

report.headline: Shoots like a good team, plays like last year's 26-win one
report.take:
Three games in, Dallas looks a lot like the team that went 26-56 last season, only with the efficiency moved to a different place. The Net Rtg of -5.9 sits almost on top of last year's -5.3, and the offensive rating of 111.3 is essentially last season's 111.2. What changed is the context: that number ranked 27th a year ago and ranks 15th now, because the league is scoring less. The 1-2 start is honest. W vs Pt Diff is 0, the margin implies exactly one win, and the two losses came by 18 at Houston and 16 at home to San Antonio.

The shot-making is real and it is top-tier: eFG % of 58.0 ranks 4th and TS % of 60.2 ranks 5th. The problem is everything around the shot. A TOV % of 16.9 ranks 27th, an FT Rate of 22.4 ranks 27th, and the ORB % of 24.8 sits well below the league. Dallas makes a lot of the shots it takes, but it doesn't take enough of them, doesn't get to the line and rarely gets second chances. That is how a top-five shooting team ends up with a middle-of-the-pack offense. On defense the frontcourt grade of D shows up: a DRB % of 67.6 ranks 26th, opponents are getting to the rim more than the league average and finishing there more often, and opposing power forwards have scored 34.67 a game, 29th in the league.

The one thing that clearly separates this team from last year's is Flagg, and so far his minutes are the whole story. He is No. 1 of 73 on the SF tab, with a 75.5 TS % on a 32 USG %, a BPM of 12.6 and an On-Off of +51.4. He has played two of the three games and is listed day-to-day. Naji Marshall, second among the wings in minutes, is out. Irving has also played in only two games, though efficiently. The guard minutes have mostly gone to Max Christie, whose 41.9 TS % and -55 On-Off are the ugliest lines on the roster. Some of this is three-game noise, but it points the right way: this team is as good as Flagg's availability and as bad as its guard and big-man depth.

Where it heads depends on which part regresses first. Hitting 36.4% from three on a low 3PA Rate is unlikely to keep producing a 58 eFG %, and if the shooting cools before the turnovers and rebounding improve, the offense drops back toward last year's bottom-five level. The upside case is a healthy Flagg playing heavy minutes, with the bad guard lineups shrinking. Even then this looks like a high-20s to mid-30s win team, not a playoff one.

strengths.title: Flagg is the best wing on the board
strengths.body: In his two games Flagg has carried a 32 USG % at a 75.5 TS %, and Dallas has been dramatically better with him on the floor. The efficiency will come down from that level over a real sample, but a No. 1 tab rank on that usage means he is the engine, not a passenger. He is the main reason the wings grade is B+ while every other group sits in D territory.

strengths.title: Elite shooting efficiency
strengths.body: Dallas ranks 4th in eFG % and 5th in TS %, well above the league averages. Irving and Sasser have both been scorching from three in limited minutes. Part of it is real shot quality from the top creators. Part of it is a hot three-game stretch from a team that takes fewer threes than the league, and that part should cool.

concerns.title: Possessions leak before shots happen
concerns.body: A 16.9 TOV % (27th), a 22.4 FT Rate (27th) and a below-league ORB % cancel out the shooting advantage and leave the offense ranked 15th. Turnovers were not a problem in any of the last five seasons, which ran in the 11-12 range, so this may partly be early-season sloppiness from a new mix. The lack of free throws and offensive rebounds, though, fits a roster built around jump shooters and a weak frontcourt.

concerns.title: Frontcourt can't end possessions
concerns.body: The frontcourt grades a D, the DRB % of 67.6 ranks 26th, and opposing power forwards are taking a far larger share of the scoring against Dallas than the league norm. P.J. Washington leads the group in minutes with a -48.2 On-Off. The bigs who have looked good, Cissé and Lawal, have barely played. Until the rotation changes, this is structural, not noise.

concerns.title: Guard minutes going to the wrong people
concerns.body: Christie leads the backcourt in minutes with a 41.9 TS % and a -55 On-Off, while Sasser has a 78 TS % and a positive On-Off in fewer minutes. With Irving having played in only two games, the backcourt grades a D+. More Irving and Sasser minutes would fix much of this.

trend.note: A loss, a 16-point win at Indiana, then a loss: three games that land almost exactly on last season's Net Rtg. There is no momentum either way yet, just a carry-over level with a better player at the top.

weekAhead.headline: Two winless bottom-feeders bracket two unbeaten heavyweights
weekAhead.body:
The week splits cleanly. Miami (0-3, last on the site) and Sacramento (0-3, 29th) are winnable, and three of the four games are at home. Oklahoma City and Houston are both 3-0 with top-eight Net Rtgs, and Houston already beat Dallas by 18 on opening night. A 2-2 week is the baseline. A sweep of the soft games is the minimum a team with Flagg should manage. Stealing one of the two hard ones would be the first real sign this isn't last year's team.

The matchups favor the shooting in the easy games and punish the turnover problem in the hard ones. Miami's perimeter defense has been the league's leakiest, and Sacramento gives up a lot to centers. Oklahoma City forces turnovers at the second-highest rate in the league and has smothered small forwards, and Houston's A+ frontcourt meets Dallas's D one on the glass.

keyMatchups.title: Thunder ball pressure vs. sloppy handling
keyMatchups.body: Oklahoma City's Opp TOV % of 18.0 ranks 2nd, and its defensive rating of 97.2 ranks 2nd. Dallas already gives the ball away at a 27th-ranked rate. Against this defense the efficient shooting may never get a chance to matter, and the Thunder have also held small forwards well below their usual output, which is aimed straight at Flagg.

keyMatchups.title: Houston rematch on the glass
keyMatchups.body: Houston's offensive rating of 122.9 ranks 3rd, and its ORB % of 31.9 ranks 8th against a Dallas DRB % that ranks 26th. Both of Houston's forward groups grade A+. This is the matchup most likely to expose the frontcourt again, as it did in the 110-128 opener.

keyMatchups.title: Soft spots in Miami and Sacramento
keyMatchups.body: Miami allows a league-worst 42.0% from three and has given shooting guards far more than their usual production, which sets up well for Irving and Sasser. Sacramento's defensive rating ranks 27th, and it has let centers outscore their usual averages by a wide margin, so Gafford should get chances. These are the games where the shooting should travel.

weekAhead.watch: Whether Flagg is cleared from day-to-day and how many minutes he plays against OKC and Houston. His on-court numbers are the difference between a 1-3 week and a 3-1 one.

restOfSeason.body:
The margin so far projects to roughly last year's level, and the sheet's pace says the same thing. What lifts Dallas above that is Flagg playing most nights with heavy usage, plus Irving getting more of the guard minutes that have gone to Christie. What drags it down is the shooting: a 58 eFG % on a low 3PA Rate and few free throws is unlikely to hold, and nothing in the rebounding or turnover profile is there to catch the offense when it cools. The defense, ranked 20th, looks like last season's 20th-ranked unit and should stay there without frontcourt help.

I expect turnovers to drift back toward this franchise's usual low-teens rates, which helps. I expect the shooting to come down toward league average, which hurts more. The net result is a team that wins more than last year's because of its best player, not because the roster underneath him has improved. Something in the range of 28 to 36 wins, with a Net Rtg still below zero, is the realistic band.
swingFactors: Whether turnovers fall back toward past seasons' rates
Frontcourt rebounding, and whether Cissé or Lawal earn real minutes

confidence.note: Three games, with Flagg, Irving and Marshall each missing time; on-off figures are tiny-sample noise.
